claim: Most antibodies have similar architectures, with the variable immunoglobulin domains of the heavy and light chain each providing three hypervariable loops, which are varied to generate diversity.
source: Nevertheless, most antibodies have similar architectures, with the variable immunoglobulin domains of the heavy and light chain each providing three hypervariable loops, which are varied to generate diversity.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge about antibody structure and is supported by the general understanding of immunology.

claim: A novel class of antibody in humans from malaria endemic regions of Africa contains one hypervariable loop with the entire collagen-binding domain of human LAIR1.
source: The recent identification of a novel class of antibody in humans from malaria endemic regions of Africa was therefore surprising as one hypervariable loop contains the entire collagen-binding domain of human LAIR1.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work (Tan et al., 2016) and is the basis for the current structural study.

claim: The antigen-binding site of the LAIR1-containing antibody has adopted an architecture that positions LAIR1 while itself being occluded.
source: We show that its antigen-binding site has adopted an architecture that positions LAIR1, while itself being occluded.
evidence: This claim is supported by the structural data presented in the manuscript, including Figure 1.

claim: The LAIR1-containing antibody represents a novel means of antigen recognition in which the Fab fragment acts as an adaptor linking a human protein insert with antigen-binding potential to the constant antibody regions.
source: This therefore represents a novel means of antigen recognition, in which the Fab fragment of an antibody acts as an adaptor, linking a human protein insert with antigen-binding potential to the constant antibody regions which mediate immune cell recruitment.
evidence: This is an interpretation based on the structural data and functional understanding presented in the manuscript.

claim: Five of the six CDRs (L1, L2, L3, H1 and H2) can be classified into a number of relatively small sets with similar lengths and architectures, and their structures are predictable from sequence.
source: While the sequences of these complementarity determining regions (CDRs) are highly variable, five of the six CDRs (L1, L2, L3, H1 and H2) can be classified into a number of relatively small sets, with similar lengths and architectures, and their structures are predictable from sequence (Chothia et al., 1989; North et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior structural studies of antibodies.

claim: The third CDR loop of the heavy chain (CDR H3) is more structurally diverse than other CDR loops, most likely due to its location close to the V(D)J recombination site.
source: In contrast, the third CDR loop of the heavy chain (CDR H3) is more structurally diverse, most likely due to its location close to the V(D)J recombination site (Weitzner et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation and represents established knowledge about antibody diversity.

claim: Human antibodies typically have CDR H3 lengths of 8–16 residues.
source: Human antibodies typically have CDR H3 lengths of 8–16 residues (Zemlin et al., 2008)
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to a prior study characterizing antibody CDR lengths.

claim: Mouse antibodies have CDR H3 lengths of 5–26 residues.
source: while mouse antibodies have CDR H3 lengths of 5–26 residues (Zemlin et al., 2003).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to a prior study characterizing antibody CDR lengths.

claim: A set of antibodies with broadly neutralizing potential against HIV have elongated third CDR loops of the heavy chain that allow them to reach through the glycan shield surrounding gp120 to bind an otherwise concealed epitope.
source: A set of antibodies with broadly neutralizing potential against HIV is one such example. Here, the third CDR loop of the heavy chain is elongated, allowing it to reach through the glycan shield that surrounds the gp120 protein to bind an otherwise concealed epitope (McLellan et al., 2011; Pancera et al., 2013; Pejchal et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to structural studies of HIV-neutralizing antibodies.

claim: Antibodies with broadly neutralizing potential against HIV are rare, making the induction of a broadly inhibitory response against HIV a major challenge.
source: Such antibodies are rare, making the induction of a broadly inhibitory response against HIV a major challenge (Corti and Lanzavecchia, 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to a review discussing HIV vaccine challenges.

claim: The majority of bovine antibodies have CDR H3 loops of around 23 residues.
source: In a more extreme example, while the majority of bovine antibodies have CDR H3 loops of around 23 residues, around 10% contain a highly elongated third CDR loop of up to 69 residues, containing a small disulphide rich domain (Saini et al., 1999; Wang et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to studies characterizing bovine antibodies.

claim: Around 10% of bovine antibodies contain a highly elongated third CDR loop of up to 69 residues, containing a small disulphide rich domain.
source: In a more extreme example, while the majority of bovine antibodies have CDR H3 loops of around 23 residues, around 10% contain a highly elongated third CDR loop of up to 69 residues, containing a small disulphide rich domain (Saini et al., 1999; Wang et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to studies characterizing bovine antibodies.

claim: The disulphide-rich domains in bovine antibodies adopt a conserved β-sheet structure that displays variable loops and are each presented on an elongated, but rigid β-hairpin.
source: These domains adopt a conserved β-sheet structure that displays variable loops and are each presented on an elongated, but rigid β-hairpin (Stanfield et al., 2016; Wang et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to structural studies of bovine antibodies.

claim: The additional domains in bovine antibodies play an important role in ligand binding.
source: While it is clear that the additional domains play an important role in ligand binding, the remaining five CDR loops are also exposed and further studies are needed to see the contribution that they make (Wang et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation and inference from structural observations.

claim: A group of unusual human antibodies in malaria endemic regions of Africa were discovered through their capacity to agglutinate human erythrocytes infected with different strains of Plasmodium falciparum.
source: A recent study identified a group of even more unusual human antibodies in malaria endemic regions of Africa (Tan et al., 2016). These antibodies were discovered through their capacity to agglutinate human erythrocytes infected with different strains of Plasmodium falciparum, and they bind to a subset of RIFIN proteins.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to the prior study that identified these antibodies.

claim: The unusual human antibodies from malaria endemic regions bind to a subset of RIFIN proteins.
source: These antibodies were discovered through their capacity to agglutinate human erythrocytes infected with different strains of Plasmodium falciparum, and they bind to a subset of RIFIN proteins.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to the prior study (Tan et al., 2016).

claim: RIFINs are displayed by the parasite on infected erythrocyte surfaces and are of uncertain function.
source: These RIFINs are displayed by the parasite on infected erythrocyte surfaces and are of uncertain function (Chan et al., 2014; Gardner et al., 1998; Kyes et al., 1999).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to studies on RIFIN proteins.

claim: The unusual antibodies show a remarkable adaptation with an intact 96 residue protein, LAIR1, inserted into the third CDR loop of the antibody heavy chain.
source: The antibodies show a remarkable adaptation with an intact 96 residue protein, LAIR1, inserted into the third CDR loop of the antibody heavy chain.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to the prior study (Tan et al., 2016) and is the basis for the current structural investigation.

claim: LAIR1 was shown to be essential for the antibody to interact with RIFINs.
source: Indeed, LAIR1 was shown to be essential for the antibody to interact with RIFINs (Tan et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to the prior functional study.

claim: The Fab fragment of antibody MGD21 was expressed in a secreted form from HEK293 cells.
source: We expressed the two chains that make up the Fab fragment of antibody MGD21 (Tan et al., 2016) in a secreted form from HEK293 cells.
evidence: This is a description of the experimental methods used in the study.

claim: Antibody MGD21 has a kappa light chain (VK1-8/JK5).
source: This antibody has a kappa light chain (VK1-8/JK5) and a heavy chain in which LAIR1 has been inserted into CDR H3.
evidence: This is a description of the antibody sequence characteristics.

claim: The MGD21 Fab fragment was crystallised and a dataset was collected to 2.52 Å resolution.
source: This fragment was purified and crystallised, allowing a dataset to be collected to 2.52 Å resolution.
evidence: This describes the experimental data collection for the structure.

claim: The structure was determined by molecular replacement using LAIR1 and the Fab fragment of antibody OX117 as search models.
source: The structure was determined by molecular replacement using LAIR1 (Brondijk et al., 2010) and the Fab fragment of antibody OX117 (Nettleship et al., 2008) as search models.
evidence: This describes the method used for structure determination with citations to the search models.

claim: Two copies of the MGD21 Fab fragment were identified in the asymmetric unit of the crystal.
source: This identified two copies of the MGD21 Fab fragment in the asymmetric unit of the crystal.
evidence: This is a result from the crystallographic analysis.

claim: A model was built for residues 2–211 of the light chain and 1–351 (with 214–219 and 264–270 disordered) of the heavy chain.
source: A model was built for residues 2–211 of the light chain and 1–351 (with 214–219 and 264–270 disordered) of the heavy chain (Figure 1, Figure 1—figure supplement 1, Figure 1—figure supplement 2, Table 1).
evidence: This describes the structural model built from the crystallographic data, with reference to figures and table.

claim: The two Fab fragments in the asymmetric unit adopt the same structure with a root mean square deviation of 0.26 Å.
source: The two Fab fragments adopt the same structure with a root mean square deviation of 0.26 Å (calculated over 475 Cα atoms) suggesting a highly ordered linkage between the variable domains of the antibody and the LAIR1 insert (Figure 1—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from structural analysis shown in the figure.

claim: The similarity between the two Fab fragments in the asymmetric unit suggests a highly ordered linkage between the variable domains of the antibody and the LAIR1 insert.
source: The two Fab fragments adopt the same structure with a root mean square deviation of 0.26 Å (calculated over 475 Cα atoms) suggesting a highly ordered linkage between the variable domains of the antibody and the LAIR1 insert (Figure 1—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the structural similarity data.

claim: The antibody sequence has three putative N-linked glycosylation sites (light chain N30; heavy chain N61 and N242).
source: The antibody sequence has three putative N-linked glycosylation sites, but of these (light chain N30; heavy chain N61 and N242) only N242 shows electron density corresponding to an Asn-linked N-acetyl glucosamine, in a position distant from the LAIR1 insert.
evidence: This is based on sequence analysis and structural observation.

claim: Only N242 shows electron density corresponding to an Asn-linked N-acetyl glucosamine, in a position distant from the LAIR1 insert.
source: The antibody sequence has three putative N-linked glycosylation sites, but of these (light chain N30; heavy chain N61 and N242) only N242 shows electron density corresponding to an Asn-linked N-acetyl glucosamine, in a position distant from the LAIR1 insert.
evidence: This is an observation from the electron density maps in the crystal structure.

claim: LAIR1 is inserted into the third CDR loop of the heavy chain through two extended linkers.
source: LAIR1 (red) is inserted into the third CDR loop of the heavy chain (yellow) through two extended linkers (orange).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1A and described in the text.

claim: LAIR1 lies across the antigen-binding surface of the variable domains of the Fab fragment.
source: The structure shows LAIR1 emerging from the CDR3 loop of the heavy chain and lying across the antigen-binding surface of the variable domains of the Fab fragment (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is a structural observation from the crystal structure shown in Figure 1A.

claim: The long axis of the LAIR1 insert is positioned with the β-strands aligned approximately perpendicular to the groove between the heavy and light chain CDRs.
source: The long axis of the LAIR1 insert is positioned with the β-strands aligned approximately perpendicular to the groove between the heavy and light chain CDRs and the insertion and linkers interact with, and occlude all five of the remaining CDR loops.
evidence: This is a structural observation from the crystal structure.

claim: The insertion and linkers interact with, and occlude all five of the remaining CDR loops.
source: The long axis of the LAIR1 insert is positioned with the β-strands aligned approximately perpendicular to the groove between the heavy and light chain CDRs and the insertion and linkers interact with, and occlude all five of the remaining CDR loops.
evidence: This is a structural observation from the crystal structure, also shown in Figure 1B.

claim: The N- and C-termini of LAIR1 lie at opposite ends of its structure, necessitating long linkers between the sites from which CDR3 emerges from the antibody heavy chain and each terminus of the LAIR1 insert.
source: The N- and C-termini of LAIR1 lie at opposite ends of its structure, necessitating long linkers between the sites from which CDR3 emerges from the antibody heavy chain and each terminus of the LAIR1 insert (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is a structural observation and logical inference from the structure shown in Figure 1A.

claim: The N-terminal linker (linker 1) is 10 residues long and adopts a simple loop structure that joins the antibody variable domain to the N-terminus of the LAIR1 insert.
source: The N-terminal linker (linker 1) is 10 residues long and adopts a simple loop structure that joins the antibody variable domain to the N-terminus of the LAIR1 insert.
evidence: This is a structural observation from the crystal structure.

claim: The C-terminal linker (linker 2) is 34 residues long and is more complex in structure.
source: The C-terminal linker (linker 2) is longer at 34 residues and is more complex in structure.
evidence: This is a structural observation from the crystal structure.

claim: Linker 2 extends out from the C-terminus of the LAIR1 insert before zigzagging back towards the insertion site in the heavy chain variable domain.
source: It extends out from the C-terminus of the LAIR1 insert before zigzagging back towards the insertion site in the heavy chain variable domain.
evidence: This is a structural observation from the crystal structure.

claim: Linker 2 is stabilized by hydrogen bonds to the LAIR1 insert and to the antibody heavy chain as well as by a disulphide bond to C93 of the antibody light chain.
source: It is stabilized by hydrogen bonds to the LAIR1 insert and to the antibody heavy chain as well as by a disulphide bond to C93 of the antibody light chain.
evidence: This is a structural observation from the crystal structure, also shown in Figure 1C and Table 2.

claim: The linkers of the LAIR1-containing antibodies sequenced to date are variable both in length and content, involving different parts of the intronic regions of the LAIR1 gene, or intergenic sequences of chromosome 13.
source: The linkers of the LAIR1-containing antibodies sequenced to date are variable both in length and content, involving different parts of the intronic regions of the LAIR1 gene, or intergenic sequences of chromosome 13 (Tan et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to the prior study that sequenced multiple antibodies.

claim: The arrangement of the linkers will in theory accommodate almost limitless variation in both length and sequence without disturbing the packing of LAIR1 against the variable domains of the antibody.
source: The arrangement of these linkers, which radiate away from the remainder of the antibody, will in theory accommodate almost limitless variation in both length and sequence without disturbing the packing of LAIR1 against the variable domains of the antibody.
evidence: This is an inference based on the structural observations and the known sequence variability.

claim: The five CDR loops lacking the LAIR1 insertion are representatives of previously identified canonical classes.
source: The five CDR loops lacking the LAIR1 insertion are representatives of previously identified canonical classes (Figure 1—figure supplement 2) (Martin and Thornton, 1996).
evidence: This is based on structural analysis and comparison with known canonical classes, supported by citation.

claim: A search using the Abcheck server identified seven unusual residues within the antibody structure: C91, C93, D97 and I106 from the light chain and Y28, R34 and Q54 from the heavy chain, all within the CDR loops.
source: However, a search using the Abcheck server (Martin, 1996) identified seven unusual residues within the antibody structure; C91, C93, D97 and I106 from the light chain and Y28, R34 and Q54 from the heavy chain, all within the CDR loops.
evidence: This is based on computational analysis using the Abcheck server, supported by citation.

claim: C91, C93 and D97 all lie in CDR3 of the light chain, perhaps facilitating its interaction with linker 2.
source: In particular, C91, C93 and D97 all lie in CDR3 of the light chain, perhaps facilitating its interaction with linker 2.
evidence: This is an inference based on the structural location of these residues and their interactions.

claim: C93 is found in only 0.096% of light chains and is the residue that forms a disulphide bond with linker 2.
source: Indeed, the most unusual residue is C93, which is found in only 0.096% of light chains, and is the residue that forms a disulphide bond with linker 2 (Figure 1B).
evidence: This combines statistical data about residue frequency with structural observation.

claim: The heavy chain CDR H3 loop has a base that adopts the 'kinked' conformation.
source: The heavy chain CDR H3 loop has a base that adopts the 'kinked' conformation (Shirai et al., 1999), with the loop rapidly spreading to the two termini of LAIR1.
evidence: This is a structural observation supported by citation to a classification system.

claim: In previous structures of antibodies with extended heavy chain CDR3 loops, the remaining five CDRs of the antibody are exposed, with the potential to engage in antigen binding.
source: In previous structures of antibodies with extended heavy chain CDR3 loops, the remaining five CDRs of the antibody are exposed, with the potential to engage in antigen binding (McLellan et al., 2011; Stanfield et al., 2016, Wang et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior structural studies of antibodies with extended CDR3 loops.

claim: One of the remarkable features of the LAIR1-containing antibody is the occlusion of large parts of each of the remaining five CDRs, with these loops each interacting directly with the LAIR1 insert and/or linkers.
source: One of the remarkable features of the LAIR1-containing antibody is therefore the occlusion of large parts of each of the remaining five CDRs, with these loops each interacting directly with the LAIR1 insert and/or linkers (Figure 1B, Table 2).
evidence: This is a structural observation from the crystal structure, shown in Figure 1B and detailed in Table 2.

claim: CDR L1 has 12.7% of its accessible surface area occluded by LAIR1 or the linkers.
source: Each of these five CDR loops was partly occluded by the presence of LAIR1 or the linkers (occluding 12.7% of the accessible surface area of CDR L1, 18.3% of CDR L2, 47.3% of CDR L3, 34.7% of CDR H1 and 16.0% of CDR H2).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from surface area calculations performed on the structure.

claim: CDR L2 has 18.3% of its accessible surface area occluded by LAIR1 or the linkers.
source: Each of these five CDR loops was partly occluded by the presence of LAIR1 or the linkers (occluding 12.7% of the accessible surface area of CDR L1, 18.3% of CDR L2, 47.3% of CDR L3, 34.7% of CDR H1 and 16.0% of CDR H2).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from surface area calculations performed on the structure.

claim: CDR L3 has 47.3% of its accessible surface area occluded by LAIR1 or the linkers.
source: Each of these five CDR loops was partly occluded by the presence of LAIR1 or the linkers (occluding 12.7% of the accessible surface area of CDR L1, 18.3% of CDR L2, 47.3% of CDR L3, 34.7% of CDR H1 and 16.0% of CDR H2).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from surface area calculations performed on the structure.

claim: CDR H1 has 34.7% of its accessible surface area occluded by LAIR1 or the linkers.
source: Each of these five CDR loops was partly occluded by the presence of LAIR1 or the linkers (occluding 12.7% of the accessible surface area of CDR L1, 18.3% of CDR L2, 47.3% of CDR L3, 34.7% of CDR H1 and 16.0% of CDR H2).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from surface area calculations performed on the structure.

claim: CDR H2 has 16.0% of its accessible surface area occluded by LAIR1 or the linkers.
source: Each of these five CDR loops was partly occluded by the presence of LAIR1 or the linkers (occluding 12.7% of the accessible surface area of CDR L1, 18.3% of CDR L2, 47.3% of CDR L3, 34.7% of CDR H1 and 16.0% of CDR H2).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from surface area calculations performed on the structure.

claim: Both the first and second CDRs of the heavy chain directly contact the LAIR1 insert.
source: Indeed, both the first and second CDRs of the heavy chain directly contact the LAIR1 insert (Table 2).
evidence: This is a structural observation detailed in Table 2.

claim: Each of the three CDR loops of the light chain interacts with one of the two linkers.
source: In addition, each of the three CDR loops of the light chain interacts with one of the two linkers, with interactions including a disulphide bond between C93 of the light chain and C223 of linker 2 (Figure 1C, Table 2).
evidence: This is a structural observation shown in Figure 1C and detailed in Table 2.

claim: There is a disulphide bond between C93 of the light chain and C223 of linker 2.
source: In addition, each of the three CDR loops of the light chain interacts with one of the two linkers, with interactions including a disulphide bond between C93 of the light chain and C223 of linker 2 (Figure 1C, Table 2).
evidence: This is a structural observation shown in Figure 1C and detailed in Table 2.

claim: The interactions between CDR loops and LAIR1/linkers are replicated in both copies of the molecule in the asymmetric unit of the crystal.
source: These interactions are replicated in both copies of the molecule in the asymmetric unit of the crystal.
evidence: This is a structural observation confirming the consistency of the interactions.

claim: The structure of MGD21 argues for a rigid association of the LAIR1 insert with the remainder of the antibody.
source: The structure of MGD21 argues for a rigid association of the LAIR1 insert with the remainder of the antibody.
evidence: This is an inference based on multiple structural observations described in the following sentences.

claim: The structures of the two molecules of the antibody in the asymmetric unit of the crystal superimpose closely.
source: Firstly, the structures of the two molecules of the antibody in the asymmetric unit of the crystal superimpose closely (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a structural observation shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: The close superimposition of the two antibody molecules is unlikely to be due solely to constraints from crystal packing.
source: It is unlikely that this is due solely to constraints from crystal packing as LAIR1 is anchored to the variable domains of the antibody through three fixed positions: the attachment sites of the two linkers, and the disulphide bond between light chain C93 and heavy chain C223 (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is an inference based on the structural features that anchor LAIR1.

claim: LAIR1 is anchored to the variable domains of the antibody through three fixed positions: the attachment sites of the two linkers, and the disulphide bond between light chain C93 and heavy chain C223.
source: It is unlikely that this is due solely to constraints from crystal packing as LAIR1 is anchored to the variable domains of the antibody through three fixed positions: the attachment sites of the two linkers, and the disulphide bond between light chain C93 and heavy chain C223 (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is a structural observation shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Each of the five CDR loops not bearing a LAIR1 insertion makes direct interactions with either LAIR1 or the linker, through contacts found in both copies of the antibody in the asymmetric unit of the crystal.
source: In addition, each of the five CDR loops not baring a LAIR1 insertion makes direct interactions with either LAIR1 or the linker, through contacts found in both copies of the antibody in the asymmetric unit of the crystal.
evidence: This is a structural observation from the crystal structure.

claim: The interactions between CDR loops and LAIR1/linkers will stabilize a tight association between LAIR1 and the antibody variable domains.
source: This will stabilize a tight association between LAIR1 and the antibody variable domains.
evidence: This is an inference based on the structural observations of multiple interactions.

claim: These antibodies can include multiple different light chains and very different linkers.
source: As these antibodies can include multiple different light chains, and very different linkers (Tan et al., 2016), these interaction will not be replicated precisely across the antibody family, but some variant of interaction between light chain CDRs and the linkers is likely.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to the prior study that characterized multiple antibodies.

claim: The interactions between light chain CDRs and linkers will not be replicated precisely across the antibody family, but some variant of interaction between light chain CDRs and the linkers is likely.
source: As these antibodies can include multiple different light chains, and very different linkers (Tan et al., 2016), these interaction will not be replicated precisely across the antibody family, but some variant of interaction between light chain CDRs and the linkers is likely.
evidence: This is an inference based on the structural observations and known sequence variability.

claim: No global structural changes have taken place in the LAIR1 insert compared to germ line LAIR1 (root mean square deviation 0.43 Å for the 82 Cα residues).
source: A comparison of the LAIR1 insert with that of the chromosomal copy of LAIR1 (referred to below as germ line) (Brondijk et al., 2010) reveals that no global structural changes have taken place (root mean square deviation 0.43 Å for the 82 Cα residues) (Figure 2A,F).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from structural comparison, shown in Figure 2A and F.

claim: The LAIR1 insertion in the MDG21 antibody differs in only 13 positions relative to the germ line sequence.
source: Indeed, the LAIR1 insertion in the MDG21 antibody differs in only 13 positions relative to the germ line sequence.
evidence: This is based on sequence comparison between the antibody LAIR1 insert and germ line LAIR1.

claim: The polymorphisms in LAIR1 do not alter residues through which the LAIR1 insert interacts with the rest of the antibody.
source: Mapping these sites onto the structure reveals that they do not alter residues through which the LAIR1 insert interacts with the rest of the antibody (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is a structural observation shown in Figure 2B.

claim: The stable interaction between LAIR1 and the antibody has come from adaptations to the CDR loops.
source: Presumably, the stable interaction between LAIR1 and the antibody has therefore come instead from adaptations to the CDR loops.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that LAIR1 polymorphisms don't affect antibody interactions.

claim: Polymorphisms in LAIR1 are mostly located on the surface distal to the rest of the antibody and have the potential to alter its interaction with collagen and with RIFIN proteins.
source: In contrast, polymorphisms are mostly located on the surface of LAIR1 distal to the rest of the antibody and have the potential to alter its interaction with its original ligand, collagen, and with the RIFIN proteins which are the target of these antibodies.
evidence: This is an inference based on the structural location of polymorphisms and knowledge of LAIR1 function.

claim: The normal function of LAIR1 is to interact with collagen.
source: The normal function of LAIR1 is to interact with collagen (Meyaard, 2008).
evidence: This is established knowledge about LAIR1 function, supported by citation.

claim: Mutations in residues R59, E61 and R65 of germ line LAIR1 have a significant impact on collagen binding.
source: In particular, mutations in residues R59, E61 and R65 have a significant impact on collagen binding (Brondijk et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to a prior mutagenesis study.

claim: The residues critical for collagen binding (R59, E61, R65) map onto the surface of LAIR1 that is most exposed in the context of the antibody.
source: These residues map onto the surface of LAIR1 (Figure 2C) that is most exposed in the context of the antibody (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is a structural observation shown in Figures 2C and 2D.

claim: Large parts of the exposed LAIR1 surface are mutable across the 27 LAIR1-containing antibodies sequenced to date.
source: Indeed, mapping of the polymorphisms found in the 27 LAIR1-containing antibodies sequenced to date shows that large parts of this surface are mutable (Figure 2E).
evidence: This is based on sequence analysis of multiple antibodies, shown in Figure 2E.

claim: The polymorphism R149N in the antibody LAIR1 insert is in the position equivalent to R65 in germ line LAIR1 and this change may impact collagen binding.
source: The polymorphisms in LAIR1 include R149N, which is in the position equivalent to R65 in germ line LAIR1 and this change may impact collagen binding.
evidence: This is an inference based on the known importance of R65 in collagen binding and the structural equivalence of R149.

claim: A polymorphism found in 7/27 of the antibodies (including MGD21) alters the N-linked glycosylation site at residue 69 of LAIR1.
source: A second polymorphism, found in 7/27 of the antibodies (including MGD21) alters the N-linked glycosyation site at residue 69 of LAIR1 (Wollscheid et al., 2009), which may alter collagen binding and/or increase RIFIN binding, but is not conserved across the antibody family.
evidence: This is based on sequence analysis of multiple antibodies and citation to a study identifying the glycosylation site.

claim: The polymorphism altering the N-linked glycosylation site at residue 69 may alter collagen binding and/or increase RIFIN binding, but is not conserved across the antibody family.
source: A second polymorphism, found in 7/27 of the antibodies (including MGD21) alters the N-linked glycosyation site at residue 69 of LAIR1 (Wollscheid et al., 2009), which may alter collagen binding and/or increase RIFIN binding, but is not conserved across the antibody family.
evidence: This is speculation about the functional consequences of the polymorphism.

claim: 11 of the 27 sequenced antibodies have mutations in at least one of the residues implicated in collagen binding, or other polymorphisms that reduce the interaction.
source: Indeed 11 of the 27 sequenced antibodies have mutations in at least one of the residues implicated in collagen binding, or other polymorphisms that reduce the interaction (Tan et al., 2016).
evidence: This is based on sequence analysis supported by citation to the prior study.

claim: The LAIR1-containing antibodies are a remarkable variant of the standard immunoglobulin fold.
source: The LAIR1-containing antibodies are a remarkable variant of the standard immunoglobulin fold.
evidence: This is an interpretive statement based on the structural findings.

claim: The third CDR of the heavy chain can accommodate unusual diversity.
source: While the majority of mammalian antibodies have predicable and short CDRs, the third CDR of the heavy chain can accommodate usual diversity (Figure 3) (McLellan et al., 2011; Wang et al., 2013; Weitzner et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior studies and shown in Figure 3.

claim: In broadly neutralizing antibodies against HIV and bovine antibodies with extended CDR3, only the heavy chain CDR3 is altered and the remaining CDR loops remain exposed for antigen binding.
source: However, in both of these cases, only the heavy chain CDR3 is altered and the remaining CDR loops remain exposed for antigen binding.
evidence: This is based on prior structural studies of these antibody types.

claim: The LAIR1-containing antibodies are an exception in that the LAIR1-insert interacts with, and partly occludes, all five of the remaining CDR loops.
source: The LAIR1-containing antibodies are an exception to this, with the LAIR1-insert interacting with, and partly occluding, all five of the remaining CDR loops.
evidence: This is based on the structural observations from this study.

claim: The structure of the LAIR1-containing antibody resembles an antibody with CDR loops adapted for LAIR1 binding, into which LAIR1 has also been inserted.
source: In many ways, the structure resembles an antibody with CDR loops adapted for LAIR1 binding, into which LAIR1 has also been inserted.
evidence: This is an interpretation based on the structural observations.

claim: The occlusion of large parts of the CDR loops by the LAIR1 insert has major consequences for its role in antigen recognition, as the majority of the antigen-binding surface will be contributed by LAIR1.
source: This occlusion of large parts of the CDR loops by the LAIR1 insert has major consequences for its role in antigen recognition, as the majority of the antigen-binding surface will be contributed by LAIR1.
evidence: This is an inference based on the structural observations of CDR occlusion.

claim: The LAIR1 insert alone can bind to infected erythrocytes.
source: Indeed, it has been shown that the LAIR1 insert alone can bind to infected erythrocytes, as can a LAIR1-containing antibody with the heavy and light chain regions exchanged (Tan et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to the prior functional study.

claim: A LAIR1-containing antibody with the heavy and light chain regions exchanged can bind to infected erythrocytes.
source: Indeed, it has been shown that the LAIR1 insert alone can bind to infected erythrocytes, as can a LAIR1-containing antibody with the heavy and light chain regions exchanged (Tan et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to the prior functional study.

claim: An antibody in which the LAIR1 insert has been exchanged for the unaltered germ line LAIR1 did not bind to erythrocytes.
source: Surprisingly an antibody in which the LAIR1 insert has been exchanged for the unaltered germ line LAIR1 did not bind to erythrocytes, although the folding of this chimera was not tested (Tan et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to the prior functional study, with a caveat about folding.

claim: The capacity of RIFINs to bind to unaltered LAIR1 alone has not yet been reported.
source: In addition, the capacity of RIFINs to bind to unaltered LAIR1 alone has not yet been reported.
evidence: This is a statement about the absence of reported data.

claim: LAIR1, or a highly related homologue, is most likely the physiological ligand of the group of RIFINs that are recognized by these antibodies.
source: Indeed, it seems most likely that LAIR1, or a highly related homologue, is the physiological ligand of the group of RIFINs that are recognized by these antibodies and that its insertion into the Fab fragment of an antibody allows it to be affinity matured to mobilise it for immune recognition and recruitment of immune cells.
evidence: This is speculation based on the structural and functional data.

claim: The insertion of LAIR1 into the Fab fragment of an antibody allows it to be affinity matured to mobilise it for immune recognition and recruitment of immune cells.
source: Indeed, it seems most likely that LAIR1, or a highly related homologue, is the physiological ligand of the group of RIFINs that are recognized by these antibodies and that its insertion into the Fab fragment of an antibody allows it to be affinity matured to mobilise it for immune recognition and recruitment of immune cells.
evidence: This is an inference about the functional advantage of the LAIR1 insertion.

claim: The LAIR1-containing antibody uses the classical hypervariable loops for a novel function: to position an inserted auxiliary domain for antigen recognition.
source: This remarkable LAIR1-containing antibody therefore uses the classical hypervariable loops for a novel function: to position an inserted auxillary domain for antigen recognition.
evidence: This is an interpretation based on the structural findings.

claim: The classical Fab fragment acts as a link between a ligand for a pathogen surface receptor and the Fc region of the antibody with its immune recruitment capability.
source: The classical Fab fragment therefore now acts as a link between a ligand for a pathogen surface receptor and the Fc region of the antibody with its immune recruitment capability.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the functional role based on the structural findings.

claim: This paradigm of using the Fab fragment to position an inserted domain may be repeated in other novel antibodies, as yet undiscovered.
source: It will be fascinating to see if this is a paradigm that is repeated in other novel antibodies, as yet undiscovered.
evidence: This is speculation about the potential generality of this mechanism.

claim: Two synthetic complementary DNA clones based on MGD21 were obtained from GeneArt.
source: Two synthetic complementary DNA clones based on MGD21 (Tan et al., 2016) were obtained from GeneArt (ThermoFisher, UK).
evidence: This is a description of the materials and methods used.

claim: The variable domains from MGD21 were fused to the constant domains derived from the pOPINVH and pOPINVL vectors.
source: Therefore the variable domains from MGD21 were fused to the constant domains derived from the pOPINVH and pOPINVL vectors.
evidence: This is a description of the construct design.

claim: DNA constructs expressing heavy and light chains were mixed in a 1 to 1 ratio and co-transfected in HEK293T cells with polyethyleneimine in the presence of 5 μM kifunensine.
source: DNA constructs expressing heavy and light chains were mixed into a 1 to 1 ratio and co-transfected in HEK293T cells (ThermoFisher Scientific, UK) with polyethyleneimine in the presence of 5 μM kifunensine (Aricescu et al., 2006).
evidence: This is a description of the expression protocol with citation to the method.

claim: After five days, conditioned media was dialysed against phosphate-buffered saline and purified by immobilised metal ion affinity chromatography using TALON resin.
source: After five days, conditioned media was dialysed against phosphate-buffered saline and purified by immobilised metal ion affinity chromatography using TALON resin (Clontech, Mountain View, CA).
evidence: This is a description of the purification protocol.

claim: The Fab heterodimer was further purified by size-exclusion chromatography using a Superdex 200 16/600 column in 10 mM HEPES, pH 7.5 and 150 mM NaCl.
source: The Fab heterodimer was further purified by size-exclusion chromatography using a Superdex 200 16/600 column (GE Healthcare Life Sciences) in 10 mM HEPES, pH 7.5 and 150 mM NaCl.
evidence: This is a description of the purification protocol.

claim: Concentrated protein (10 mg/ml) was incubated with Flavobacterium meningosepticum endoglycosidase-F1 for in situ deglycosylation.
source: Concentrated protein (10 mg/ml) was incubated with Flavobacterium meningosepticum endoglycosidase-F1 for in situ deglycosylation (Hsieh et al., 2016).
evidence: This is a description of the crystallization preparation with citation to the method.

claim: The protein crystals were obtained in 20% (w/v) PEG4000, 0.1 M sodium citrate, pH 4.5 at 18°C.
source: The protein crystals were obtained in 20% (w/v) PEG4000, 0.1 M sodium citrate, pH 4.5 at 18°C.
evidence: This is a description of the crystallization conditions.

claim: Crystals were transferred into mother liquor containing 25% (w/v) glycerol and were then cryo-cooled in liquid nitrogen for storage and data collection.
source: Crystals were transferred into mother liquor containing 25% (w/v) glycerol and were then cryo-cooled in liquid nitrogen for storage and data collection.
evidence: This is a description of the crystal handling protocol.

claim: Data were collected on beamline I04-1 at the Diamond Light Source.
source: Data were collected on beamline I04-1 at the Diamond Light Source and were indexed and scaled using XDS (Kabsch, 2010).
evidence: This is a description of the data collection location.

claim: Data were indexed and scaled using XDS.
source: Data were collected on beamline I04-1 at the Diamond Light Source and were indexed and scaled using XDS (Kabsch, 2010).
evidence: This is a description of the data processing method with citation.

claim: Phaser was used to determine a molecular replacement model.
source: Phaser (McCoy et al., 2007) was used to determine a molecular replacement model, using the known structures of LAIR1 (pdb: 3KGR (Brondijk et al., 2010)) and a human monoclonal antibody Fab fragment similar to MGD21 (pdb: 3DIF, (Nettleship et al., 2008)) separated into two files containing the variable and the constant regions, as search models.
evidence: This is a description of the structure determination method with citations.

claim: Refinement and rebuilding was completed using Buster and Coot respectively.
source: Refinement and rebuilding was completed using Buster (Blanc et al., 2004) and Coot (Emsley et al., 2010) respectively.
evidence: This is a description of the refinement methods with citations.

claim: AREAIMOL from the CCP4 suite was used to determine the accessible surface area of each CDR loop both in the presence and absence of LAIR1 and the linkers.
source: To determine the effect of the LAIR1 insert on the accessible surface area of the CDR loops, we used AREAIMOL from the CCP4 suite (Winn et al., 2011) to determine the accessible surface area of each CDR loop both in the presence and absence of LAIR1 and the linkers.
evidence: This is a description of the analysis method with citation.
